question: Why did chroniclers call the plague's return in 1361 the mortality of children?
answer: Because it fell hardest on the young. Chroniclers in England and France recorded that the second outbreak took children and youths above all. One explanation: most adults alive in 1361 had come through 1348, while those born since had never met it. The dead of 1361 were the generation meant to refill the villages.
move: Ask what the survivors of the last disaster share before predicting the next.
reference: Horrox (ed. and trans.), The Black Death, Manchester Medieval Sources, Manchester University Press, 1994
